files.name: CLAUDE.md
files.description: Master orchestrator that runs the baseline once and the weekly smoke test on demand.
files.content:
# Automation Smoke Test — Orchestrator

You run a weekly health check over a set of n8n automations. Your job is to catch two failures: a workflow that stopped firing (went quiet) and a workflow that started erroring. You read logs and you report. You never edit, disable, or re-run a workflow.

## What this system does
Silent failures are the expensive ones. A workflow that throws a red error tells you it broke. A workflow that quietly stops firing tells you nothing, and every lead or order that ran through it falls on the floor until someone notices. This system catches that by learning each workflow's normal cadence once, then checking against it every week.

## Files you read
- `context/n8n-connection.md` — the user's n8n URL and API key. Read this first, every time.
- `context/thresholds.md` — tunable settings: quiet multiplier, error cutoffs, low-sample guard, run day.
- `system/baseline-skill.md` — the procedure that learns normal cadence. Run once, re-run monthly.
- `system/smoke-test-skill.md` — the weekly check procedure. Run every friday.
- `system/tag-reference.md` — the two signals, what each tag means, and how to write the report.

## Workflow
1. Check whether `automation-baseline.json` exists in this folder.
   - If it does not exist: run `system/baseline-skill.md` end to end. This learns the normal cadence for every active workflow and writes `automation-baseline.json`. Then stop and tell the user the baseline is set and they can run the smoke test now.
   - If it exists: continue to step 2.
2. Run `system/smoke-test-skill.md`. It reads recent executions, compares against the baseline, and tags each workflow.
3. Apply the tag rules and severity order from `system/tag-reference.md`.
4. Write the report per the output format below.

## Output format
One screen, flagged items on top:
- Header line: healthy count, flagged count, the single workflow to open first.
- Then DEAD, then ERRORING, then NOISY, then UNREACHABLE.
- Skip HEALTHY workflows except the count in the header.
- Every row shows: workflow name, last run time, minutes since last run vs threshold, error rate, and the workflow id in brackets.
- End on one line: how many healthy, how many flagged, which one to open first.

## Rules
- Read only. Never edit, disable, or re-run a workflow.
- If a workflow's API call fails, tag it UNREACHABLE and treat it as DEAD until proven otherwise. A workflow you cannot read is its own kind of dead.
- Keep the whole report under one screen. The point is a 15-minute scan, not an audit.
- Re-run the baseline monthly, or whenever the user adds or removes workflows.

files.description: Two-minute setup guide for the kit.
files.content:
# Automation Smoke Test Kit

A 15-minute weekly health check that catches n8n workflows which silently stopped firing or started erroring, before a client asks why something didn't happen.

## What it does
One of my automations quit on a monday and stayed dead till thursday. No error, no alert. I found it because a lead never got its follow-up. This kit is the check I built so that never costs me a client call again. It learns what normal looks like for each workflow, then flags the ones that went quiet or started failing.

## Quick start
1. Fill in `context/n8n-connection.md` with your n8n URL and API key. Adjust `context/thresholds.md` if you want, the defaults work.
2. Open this folder in Claude Code and say: run the baseline. It reads 30 days of history and writes `automation-baseline.json`. Do this once.
3. Every friday, say: run the smoke test. You get a one-screen report grouped by severity. Read it, fix what's flagged, done.

## The files
- `CLAUDE.md` — the orchestrator. Tells Claude Code how to run the two steps in order.
- `context/n8n-connection.md` — your instance URL and API key. You fill this in.
- `context/thresholds.md` — the tunable knobs: how patient the quiet check is, where the error line sits. You fill this in.
- `system/baseline-skill.md` — the procedure that learns each workflow's normal cadence. Run once, re-run monthly.
- `system/smoke-test-skill.md` — the weekly check. Reads logs, compares to baseline, tags each workflow.
- `system/tag-reference.md` — what DEAD, ERRORING, NOISY, and UNREACHABLE mean and what to do about each.

## Customization
- Change the quiet multiplier in `context/thresholds.md`. Default is 3x the median gap. Drop it to 2x for earlier warnings and a few more false flags, raise to 4x if your run times are lumpy.
- Move the error cutoff. Default draws urgent at 25% of the last 20 runs. It's held up across my own 30 automations. Watch a few weeks of reports before you touch it.
- Run it any day. Friday is just when I do it.

---
{{CREDIT_LINE}}

files.name: n8n-connection.md
files.description: User-filled n8n instance URL, API key, and optional workflow scope.
files.content:
# n8n Connection

Fill in your own values. Both skills read this file before they call the API.

## Instance URL
Your self-hosted or cloud n8n base URL, no trailing slash.

BASE_URL: [https://your-n8n.example.com]

Example:
BASE_URL: https://n8n.yourcompany.com

## API key
Create one in n8n under Settings > n8n API. Read access is enough. This system never writes.

API_KEY: [paste-your-n8n-api-key-here]

The key goes in the request header on every call:
X-N8N-API-KEY: {API_KEY}

## Scope (optional)
By default both skills check every active workflow. If you only want to watch a few, list their ids here and tell Claude to check only these. Leave blank to check everything active.

WATCH_ONLY: [leave blank for all active workflows]

Example:
WATCH_ONLY: Tj2AhYmAFQ9rCgyp, dk498RKEZME1MjDX

files.name: thresholds.md
files.description: User-tunable knobs: quiet multiplier, error cutoffs, low-sample guard, run day.
files.content:
# Thresholds

Two knobs, a guard, and a schedule. The defaults work out of the box. Change them once you've watched a few weekly reports.

## Quiet multiplier
How patient the "went quiet" check is. The baseline records each workflow's median gap between runs. The quiet threshold is this multiplier times that median.

QUIET_MULTIPLIER: [3]

- 3 is the default and where I run mine.
- Drop to 2 for earlier warnings. Expect a few more false flags on lumpy workflows.
- Raise to 4 if your run times are naturally uneven and 3x flags things that were fine.

Example: median gap 60 min at 3x means flagged after 180 min quiet.

## Error cutoffs
Read across the last 20 runs of each workflow.

ERRORING_CUTOFF: [25]   percent of last 20 runs failing = urgent
NOISY_FLOOR: [5]        percent between this and the cutoff = worth noting

- 25% is where I draw urgent. It's held up across my own 30 automations.
- Under 5% failing is treated as healthy.

## Low-sample guard
A workflow with fewer than this many runs in 30 days can't give a trustworthy median. It gets marked low_sample and you set its threshold by hand.

MIN_SAMPLE: [5]

## Run day
A reminder to yourself. The smoke test runs whenever you tell it to.

RUN_DAY: [friday]

files.name: baseline-skill.md
files.description: The pre-built baseline procedure that learns each workflow's normal cadence.
files.content:
# System: Baseline Skill

Run this once before the first smoke test, then re-run monthly as your stack changes. It reads 30 days of execution history and records how often each active workflow normally runs. The smoke test compares against this to catch a workflow that went quiet.

## Why cadence first
"Stopped firing" only means something if you know how often the workflow is supposed to fire. A weekly report going quiet for 3 days is fine. An hourly sync going quiet for 3 days is a fire. So you need a baseline per workflow before you can check anything.

## Skill definition
Paste this as a Claude Code skill, or just follow the steps below.

---
name: automation-baseline
description: Learns the normal run cadence for every active n8n workflow so the weekly smoke test knows what "quiet" looks like. Run once, then re-run monthly.
---

## Steps
1. Read `context/n8n-connection.md` for BASE_URL and API_KEY. Read `context/thresholds.md` for QUIET_MULTIPLIER and MIN_SAMPLE.

2. GET {BASE_URL}/api/v1/workflows?active=true
   Header: X-N8N-API-KEY: {API_KEY}
   Keep id and name for each active workflow. If WATCH_ONLY is set, keep only those ids.

3. For each workflow:
   GET {BASE_URL}/api/v1/executions?workflowId={id}&limit=100
   Same header. Pull the startedAt timestamp of every run.

4. Sort the timestamps. Compute the gap in minutes between each run and the one before it. Take the MEDIAN gap. That median is the normal cadence.

5. Set the quiet threshold at QUIET_MULTIPLIER times the median gap (default 3x). A workflow that has not run in longer than its threshold is a candidate for "went quiet".
   - median 60 min  -> threshold 180 min
   - median 1 day   -> threshold 3 days
   - weekly runs    -> threshold ~21 days

6. Write `automation-baseline.json`, one row per workflow: id, name, median_gap_minutes, quiet_threshold_minutes, sample_size.

7. If a workflow has fewer than MIN_SAMPLE runs in 30 days, mark it low_sample: true and set its threshold by hand. Do not trust a median off 2 data points.

8. Print a table: workflow name, cadence in plain English (every ~1 hour / every ~day / weekly), and its threshold.

## The math, so you can check it by hand
Take the timestamps of the last runs, measure the gap between each one, take the median gap, set the quiet threshold at 3x that median. Median gap 60 minutes gives a 180 minute threshold. A weekly workflow has a median gap around 10,080 minutes, so its threshold lands near 21 days, which is 30,240 minutes.

## File shape
`automation-baseline.json` is the memory the smoke test reads every week:

```json
{
  "baselines": [
    {
      "id": "Tj2AhYmAFQ9rCgyp",
      "name": "Lead follow-up sender",
      "median_gap_minutes": 60,
      "quiet_threshold_minutes": 180,
      "sample_size": 100,
      "low_sample": false
    },
    {
      "id": "Id1IDV5t9kUpwjVH",
      "name": "Weekly topic research",
      "median_gap_minutes": 10080,
      "quiet_threshold_minutes": 30240,
      "sample_size": 4,
      "low_sample": true
    }
  ]
}
```

files.name: smoke-test-skill.md
files.description: The pre-built weekly check that reads logs, compares to baseline, and tags workflows.
files.content:
# System: Weekly Smoke Test Skill

This is the skill I run every friday. It reads the logs, compares against the baseline, and writes a short report grouped by severity. You read it, fix what's flagged, done.

## Skill definition
Paste this as a Claude Code skill, or just follow the steps below.

---
name: weekly-smoke-test
description: The 15-minute Friday health check. Reads n8n execution logs, flags any active workflow that stopped firing or started erroring, and writes a short report to approve or ignore.
---

## Steps
1. Load `automation-baseline.json`. If it is missing, tell the user to run the baseline skill first, then stop.

2. Read `context/n8n-connection.md` for BASE_URL and API_KEY. Read `context/thresholds.md` for ERRORING_CUTOFF and NOISY_FLOOR.

3. GET {BASE_URL}/api/v1/workflows?active=true
   Header: X-N8N-API-KEY: {API_KEY}
   Note any workflow active now but not in the baseline (new since last baseline) and any baseline workflow no longer active (someone turned it off).

4. For each active workflow:
   GET {BASE_URL}/api/v1/executions?workflowId={id}&limit=20
   Same header.

5. Compute two numbers per workflow:
   - Minutes since last run = now minus the newest startedAt
   - Error rate = (runs with status error or crashed) / (runs pulled)

6. Tag each workflow:
   - DEAD:     minutes since last run > quiet_threshold_minutes
   - ERRORING: error rate >= ERRORING_CUTOFF (default 25%) across the last 20 runs
   - NOISY:    error rate between NOISY_FLOOR and ERRORING_CUTOFF (default 5% to 25%)
   - HEALTHY:  ran within threshold, error rate under NOISY_FLOOR

7. Write the report DEAD first, then ERRORING, then NOISY. Skip HEALTHY except for a count at the top. For each flagged workflow show: name, last run time, minutes since last run vs threshold, error rate, and the id.

8. End with one line: how many healthy, how many flagged, and the single workflow you would open first.

## Rules
- Read only. This skill never edits or re-runs a workflow. It reports.
- If a workflow's API call fails, tag it UNREACHABLE and list it. A workflow you cannot read is its own kind of dead.
- Keep the whole report under one screen. The point is a 15-minute scan.

files.name: tag-reference.md
files.description: The methodology: the two signals read, tag meanings, severity order, and report shape.
files.content:
# System: Tag Reference

This is the read layer. It defines the two signals the smoke test reads, what each tag means, and the shape of the report.

## The two signals
Everything else is noise. These two catch the failures that actually cost you something.

| Signal | Question it answers | How it's measured |
|---|---|---|
| Went quiet | Did this workflow stop firing? | Minutes since last run vs its normal cadence |
| Started erroring | Is this workflow failing more than usual? | Error rate across the last 20 runs |

- Went quiet catches the monday-to-thursday death: no runs, no errors, nothing in the log to trip an alert.
- Started erroring catches the workflow that runs but fails halfway, so half your leads get processed and half don't.
- Both together give you a one-screen report you can read in the time it takes to drink a coffee.

## How to read the tags

| Tag | What it means | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| DEAD | Stopped firing past its normal cadence | Open it now. This is the silent failure. |
| ERRORING | Failing 1 in 4 runs or worse | Open the last errored run, read the failing node |
| NOISY | Occasional failures, under 25% | Note it. Fix if it climbs next week. |
| UNREACHABLE | The check couldn't read it | Treat as DEAD until proven otherwise |

A DEAD tag on a workflow that ran fine last week is the one that saves you a client call. That's the exact failure I missed for three days.

## Severity order
Always write flagged items on top: DEAD, then ERRORING, then NOISY, then UNREACHABLE. Fold every healthy workflow into a single count in the header. Put the workflow id on every row so the reader can open it without hunting.

## Report shape
The output reads in one pass:

```
SMOKE TEST, friday scan
23 healthy · 3 flagged · look at "Lead follow-up sender" first

DEAD (stopped firing)
- Lead follow-up sender  [Tj2AhYmAFQ9rCgyp]
  last run 4 days ago · threshold 180 min · 0 runs since monday

ERRORING (>=25% failing)
- 3PL order router  [dk498RKEZME1MjDX]
  last run 20 min ago · 7 of last 20 runs errored (35%)

NOISY (5-25% failing)
- Klaviyo notify  [0zD6WZRBD7FnaAhw]
  last run 1 hr ago · 2 of last 20 runs errored (10%)

UNREACHABLE
- (none)
```

## Two settings to tune
The 3x quiet multiplier controls how patient the went-quiet check is. Drop it to 2x for earlier warnings and a few false flags, raise to 4x if run times are lumpy. The 25% error cutoff is where urgent gets drawn, and it's held up across my own 30 automations. Both live in `context/thresholds.md`. Watch a few weeks of reports before you move either one.
